ideas.title: FT8 for POTA: The Mode That Keeps You Busy in the Field
ideas.why_now: Multiple activators this week reported FT8 pileups and 80-QSO nights on 40m, and FT8 velocity is climbing.
ideas.angle: Walk through the practical setup for running FT8 during a POTA activation: apps, split operation, logging on the fly, and when to switch back to SSB when the pile gets deep enough.

ideas.title: Chasing PQ1I: How to Work a DXpedition as an Everyday Ham
ideas.why_now: PQ1I from Ilha das Garcas SA-067 is trending new this week with multiple QRZ threads lighting up around it.
ideas.angle: Use this active DXpedition as a teachable moment: how to find spots, pick the right band and time, manage a pileup call, and confirm the contact afterward without losing your mind.

sources.label: QRZ Forums, PQ1I Ilha Das Garcas SA-067
QRZ Forums, PQ1I Espirito Santo State Group SA-067

ideas.title: 16 Parks in One Day: Planning an Ambitious POTA Run
ideas.why_now: An operator posted this week about attempting 23 parks in a single day, completing 16 with 130 contacts, sparking real discussion about planning and pacing.
ideas.angle: Break down how to plan a multi-park day: route scouting, quick-deploy antenna choices, logging discipline, and how to know when to cut your losses and drive to the next stop.

sources.label: Mastodon, 16 parks activated in one day, 130 contacts
Mastodon @tdr112, 3 parks in one in Galway

ideas.title: The Xiegu G7250: What a 100W SDR Desktop Rig Means for the Rest of Us
ideas.why_now: The Xiegu G7250 was announced this week: 100W, split SDR design, 7-inch touchscreen, targeting the mid-market.
ideas.angle: Give an accessible first look at the specs and discuss what this kind of rig means for hams who want modern SDR features without flagship pricing, and whether it fits a portable or home shack build.

ideas.title: Greyline Operating: A Simple Trick That Makes 20m Come Alive
ideas.why_now: Greyline propagation is the focus of this week's HamChallenge, and 20m is trending new this week with reports of DX to Australia and Japan.
ideas.angle: Explain greyline in plain terms, show how to find your window with free tools, and give a simple plan for getting on 20m at the right moment even with modest gear.

sources.label: Mastodon @ChrisHolladay, Australia and Japan on 20m and 17m

ideas.title: Ham Radio at DEF CON and HOPE: The Hacker Path Into the Hobby
ideas.why_now: DEF CON and HOPE are both running Ham-In-A-Day licensing courses this summer, opening a fresh on-ramp for tech-curious newcomers.
ideas.angle: Talk about the overlap between the hacker and ham communities, what draws technically-minded people into the hobby, and how clubs can welcome this crowd rather than intimidate them.

sources.label: Mastodon @sergio_101, two young newcomers asking for license help

ideas.title: HamSCI Meteor Scatter QSO Party: Science You Can Do From Your Radio
ideas.why_now: The first 2026 HamSCI Meteor Scatter QSO Party runs July 29-31, giving operators a short window to participate in real citizen science.
ideas.angle: Explain what meteor scatter is, what HamSCI is collecting from participants, and what a basic station needs to join in. Frame it as one of the coolest things a ham can do on a random Tuesday night.

sources.label: QRZ Forums, HamSCI Meteor Scatter QSO Party July 29-31 2026

ideas.title: Women in Ham Radio: Why the Gap Exists and What We Can Do

ideas.angle: Have an honest, non-preachy conversation about why the hobby skews so heavily and what everyday operators and clubs can actually do to make the welcome mat feel real, not performative.
